newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine T-bill trading quiet as banks bide time.
newsitem.headline: Philippine T-bill trading quiet as banks bide time.

text.p: There were few buyers in the secondary market for Philippine Treasury bills as fears of rising interest rates persisted, traders said on Friday.
"There were a lot of sellers, but no buyer in sight," one trader at an investment house said.
He said the prolonged uncertainties in the peso-dollar market as a result of the continued attack on regional currencies had prompted the central bank to keep its benchmark rates firm.
"Untill the central bank keeps its rates at these levels, we might still see some uptick in the T-bills," he said.
The lower T-bills offering at Monday's auction could temper the rise though, he added.
Bid-offer quotes for T-bills remained wide, signalling a confused market. Three-month bills were being bid between 13.5 to 14.0 percent and offered at 13.1 to 13.5 percent.
Bids for one-year bills were at 14.25 to 14.625 percent, while offers were at 13.1 to 14.0 percent.

Short-term 35-day and 42-day bills were heavily traded with done rates ranging between 16.75 to 17.0 percent, much lower than the average 17.558 percent for the 35-day bills and 17.283 percent for the 42-days.
The interbank call loan rate was unchanged at 25.03125 percent amid sluggish turnover of 9.926 billion pesos.
